common.propsOffWarning: Remove all propellers before connecting the battery.

demo.title: Demo mode.
demo.bodySome: Some features are simulated: this app version cannot do them on a real flight controller yet, so nothing is read from or written to the board for them.
demo.bodyAll: Everything runs on a simulated flight controller. Nothing is read from or written to a real board.

welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.body: This wizard flashes Betaflight and configures your flight controller step by step, no website needed.

connect.title: Connect
connect.description: Plug the flight controller into the computer with a USB data cable.

firmware.title: Firmware
firmware.description: Check that the board runs a recent Betaflight version, and update it if needed.

components.title: What is connected?
components.description: Tell us what is wired to the flight controller. We only ask about the parts you have.

receiver.title: Receiver
receiver.description: The receiver gets the commands from your radio.

binding.title: Binding
binding.description: Pair the receiver with your transmitter.

vtx.title: Video transmitter
vtx.description: Lets the flight controller change video channel and power from your radio or goggles.

gps.title: GPS
gps.description: Used for rescue mode and position on the OSD.

esc.title: ESC & motors
esc.description: How the flight controller talks to the motors.

switches.title: Switches
switches.description: Choose which switch on your radio arms the quad and turns on flight modes.

review.title: Review
review.description: Check everything before it is written to the board. Nothing has been changed yet.

apply.title: Apply
apply.description: Write the settings to the flight controller and check that they stuck.

calibration.title: Sensors and level
calibration.description: Check the sensors, calibrate the accelerometer, and make sure the board knows which way it is mounted.

beepers.title: Beeps
beepers.description: Choose when the quad beeps. Beeps tell you about the battery and the radio link, and help you find a crashed quad.

osd.title: Screen overlay (OSD)
osd.description: Choose what you see on top of the video in your goggles.

welcome.need1: The flight controller, with all propellers removed.
welcome.need2: A USB cable that carries data (not a charge-only cable).
welcome.need3: Your radio, bound to the receiver, if you have one.

connect.step1: Plug in the flight controller with a USB cable. The battery is needed later, for the motor test.
connect.step2: Choose it in the list, or let the wizard find it.
connect.dfuTitle: The board is in flashing (DFU) mode
connect.dfuBody: It can be flashed, but not configured, in this mode. Continue to the firmware step, or unplug and replug it to start it normally.
connect.driverHelpTitle: The board does not show up?
connect.driverHelp1: Try another cable or USB port. Many cables only charge.
connect.driverHelp2: On Windows a driver may be missing. The wizard can install it for you.

firmware.unsupportedTitle: This firmware is too old for the wizard
firmware.unsupportedBody: The wizard supports Betaflight {min} and newer. Update the firmware to continue.
firmware.upToDate: Your firmware is up to date.
firmware.releasesUnavailable: The list of versions is not available offline. You can keep the current firmware.
firmware.releasesFailed: Could not load the list of versions.
firmware.backupNote: Your current settings are backed up before the update.
firmware.doNotUnplug: Do not unplug the board until this finishes.
firmware.droppedIntro: This firmware version doesn't include some features of the board's old firmware:
firmware.droppedAfter: These features were left out. Settings that use them won't work with this firmware.
firmware.notSupportedYetTitle: The wizard can't set up this Betaflight version yet
firmware.notSupportedYetBody: This board has Betaflight {version}. This version of the wizard can't set it up yet. Install one of the versions below to continue, or check for a newer version of the wizard.
firmware.lineNotSupported: not supported by the wizard yet
firmware.someNotSupported: Versions marked “not supported by the wizard yet” can't be picked: the wizard can't set them up yet.

readProtect.title: This board is locked (read protection)
readProtect.what: The chip on this flight controller has read protection turned on. Some boards ship like this from the factory, or after someone used other flashing tools. While it is on, new firmware cannot be written.
readProtect.why: Nothing has been changed on the board so far.
readProtect.eraseWarning: Removing the protection ERASES THE WHOLE CHIP. This cannot be undone.
readProtect.lose1: The current firmware is deleted. The board will not fly until the new firmware is flashed, which the wizard does right after.
readProtect.lose2: All settings stored on the board are deleted.
readProtect.backupSaved: A backup of your settings was saved before the update. You can restore it from Backups.
readProtect.noBackup: No backup of the board's settings could be saved, so they cannot be restored afterwards.
readProtect.safe: This is the normal way to unlock a board and does not damage it. Keep the USB cable plugged in until flashing is finished.
readProtect.understand: I understand that everything on the chip will be erased.
readProtect.erase: Erase the chip and continue flashing
readProtect.leave: Don't want to erase it? Unplug the board. Nothing on it has been changed.

rxKindHint.SERIAL: For example ExpressLRS, Crossfire, TBS, FrSky or FlySky receivers.
rxKindHint.SPI: Your board reports a built-in ExpressLRS receiver.
rxKindHint.NONE: You need a receiver to fly. You can come back later.

vtxKindHint.DIGITAL: Shows the OSD in your goggles.
vtxKindHint.ANALOG: Change channel and power from the OSD menu.
vtxKindHint.NONE: The video transmitter is not connected to a UART.

components.gpsHint: Enables GPS rescue and position on the OSD.
components.escTelemetryHint: Only if a telemetry wire from the ESC goes to a UART. Not needed with bidirectional DShot.
components.softSerialNote: Soft serial ports are not supported in this version.

receiver.telemetryQuestion: Send telemetry (battery, signal) back to the radio?
receiver.telemetryHint: Telemetry shows battery voltage and link quality on your radio.
receiver.elrsHint: With ExpressLRS, the arm switch must be on AUX1.
receiver.onboardBody: No UART is needed. Bind it to your radio after setup.
receiver.optionMissing: The firmware on this board doesn't include {protocol} receivers (missing: {options}).
receiver.optionMissingChoices: Pick the protocol your receiver really uses, or update the firmware to add this one.
receiver.optionMissingApplied: You can't continue with {protocol}: the firmware on this board doesn't include it, and the firmware can't be updated now because settings were already written to the board in this session. Pick the protocol your receiver really uses. To use {protocol}, finish the wizard, update the firmware, then run the wizard again.
receiver.optionMissingNoUpdate: You can't continue with {protocol}: the firmware on this board doesn't include it, and the firmware can't be updated from the wizard right now (for example, because part of the data here is simulated). Pick the protocol your receiver really uses. To use {protocol}, update the firmware first, then run the wizard again.

binding.familyQuestion: Which radio system is this receiver?
binding.crossfireNote: Crossfire and Tracer receivers are bound from the transmitter's TBS menu (or TBS Agent). There is nothing to set here.
binding.what: ExpressLRS pairs the receiver with your transmitter using a binding phrase: a word or sentence you choose, a bit like a Wi-Fi password.
binding.mustMatch: It must be exactly the same as the phrase on your transmitter: same letters, capitals and spaces. Otherwise they will not connect.
binding.whereToFind: You set it when the transmitter's ExpressLRS module was flashed (for example in ExpressLRS Configurator). If you don't know it, choose the bind button instead.
binding.howQuestion: How do you want to bind?
binding.useButton: Skip the phrase and bind with the button
binding.phraseLabel: Binding phrase (same as on your transmitter)
binding.spacesWarning: The phrase starts or ends with a space. That is allowed, but it must be the same on the transmitter.
binding.notSaved: The phrase is not saved anywhere. The app turns it into a short code for the receiver and then forgets it.
binding.phraseSet: Binding phrase set. It will be written to the flight controller when you apply the settings. The phrase itself was not saved.
binding.uartPhrase: This receiver is connected with wires and keeps its own binding phrase. The flight controller cannot change it, so set the same phrase on the receiver itself:
binding.uartPhrase1: In ExpressLRS Configurator, enter the phrase when you flash the receiver, or
binding.uartPhrase2: Turn on the receiver's Wi-Fi (ExpressLRS Lua script on the transmitter: WiFi Connectivity → Enable Rx WiFi) and enter the phrase on its web page.
binding.buttonSpi1: Put the flight controller's receiver in bind mode: press its bind button (see the board's manual; it is not the BOOT button), or use Bind on the Receiver tab of the Betaflight app.
binding.buttonUart1: Put the receiver in bind mode: plug the quad in and unplug it three times in a row (each time less than a second), or press the button on the receiver. Its light blinks twice quickly.
binding.button2: On the transmitter, open the ExpressLRS Lua script and choose Bind.
binding.button3: When the light on the receiver stays on, it is bound.
binding.buttonSpiKeep: The wizard keeps the board's current binding. You can bind after applying the settings.
binding.buttonLater: You can do this any time after the wizard is finished.

vtx.digitalHint: Digital systems use MSP DisplayPort for the OSD.

gps.hint: Most modules use UBLOX. Wire GPS TX to the UART RX pad and GPS RX to TX.

esc.bidirHint: Needs ESC firmware that supports it (BLHeli_32, Bluejay, AM32).
esc.polesHint: Count the magnets on the motor bell. Most 5 inch motors have 14.
esc.propsOutHint: Only if your frame setup uses props out.
esc.reverseHint: Changing the spin direction of one motor will be added later.

motorTest.title: Motor test
motorTest.warning: Motors will spin. Confirm both before testing:
motorTest.keepClear: Keep hands, hair and loose objects clear of the motors, and hold or secure the quad while they spin.
motorTest.ackBatteryHint: The ESCs need battery power to spin the motors. Hold or secure the quad and keep clear of the motors.
motorTest.unavailable: The motor test is not available in this version yet. You can skip it and check the motors later in Betaflight Configurator, with the propellers removed.
motorTest.diagram: Motor layout, seen from above, front at the top
motorTest.running: Motor {n} is spinning. Select it again or Stop to stop it.
motorTest.stopNote: Motors stop when you leave this step or switch windows, when you close the window or quit the app, and on their own within half a second if the app stops responding.
motorTest.noSpinBody: Check that the battery is connected and the ESCs are powered (most ESCs beep when they get power), and that the ESCs are plugged into the flight controller. Then select the motor again.
motorTest.checkIntro: Recommended: spin each motor and tick what you see. It catches swapped motor wires before the first flight.
motorTest.orderOk: The right motor spins for each button.
motorTest.directionOk: Every motor spins in the direction shown.

advancedChecks.title: Advanced ESC checks
advancedChecks.note: These checks are not in this version yet. You can do them later in Betaflight Configurator, with the propellers removed.

switches.namesNew: Mode names for Betaflight {version} and newer.
switches.liveHint: Flip the switches on your radio: the active mode lights up.
switches.liveUnavailable: Live switch display is not available yet. Choose the switches from the lists.
switches.liveStopped: The live switch display stopped. Check the connection.
switches.armHint: Arming starts the motors. Use a switch that is hard to flip by accident.
switches.detectHint: Flip the switch you want to use for this mode on your radio. The wizard picks the channel that moves.

prearm.title: Prearm: a second safety switch (optional)
prearm.body: With prearm, the quad only arms if this switch is on first. It protects against arming by accident, for example when you bump the arm switch while carrying the quad.
prearm.addHint: A switch row is added above. Arm only works after this switch is on.
prearm.skipHint: The wizard does not change prearm. If the board already has a prearm switch, it stays.
prearm.removeHint: If the board already has a prearm switch, it is removed. If it has none, nothing changes.

turtle.title: Turtle mode: flip over after a crash (optional)
turtle.body: If the quad lands upside down, turtle mode spins the motors backwards so you can flip it back over and fly on, without walking to it.
turtle.needsDshot: Turtle mode needs the DShot ESC protocol. Your ESC is not set to DShot, so it will not work.
turtle.dshotOk: Your ESC uses DShot, so turtle mode can work.
turtle.added: Turtle mode is on a switch above.

airmode.title: Air mode
airmode.body: Air mode keeps the quad stable and under control even with the throttle all the way down, for example in flips, rolls and dives. Most pilots keep it always on.
airmode.alwaysHint: Air mode is on whenever the quad is armed.
airmode.switchHint: Turn air mode on and off with a switch. A switch row is added above.
airmode.offHint: At zero throttle the quad may wobble or drop and is harder to control.
airmode.keepHint: The wizard does not change air mode.

switches.removeExisting: If the board already has a switch for {mode}, remove it
switches.removeHint: The wizard cannot see which switches the board has now. Removing a switch the board does not have changes nothing.

sensors.title: Sensors on your board
sensors.unavailable: This app version cannot read the sensors yet. The board keeps its current sensor settings.
sensors.simulated: The sensor list is from the demo, not from your board, so these choices will not be written.
sensors.gyroHint: Measures how fast the quad turns. The quad cannot fly without it, so it is always on.
sensors.accHint: Knows which way is down. Needed for the self-level modes (Angle, Horizon) and some GPS features.
sensors.baroHint: Measures air pressure to estimate height. Needed for altitude hold.
sensors.keepHint: If you do not change anything here, the board keeps its current sensor settings.
sensors.offHint: Turned off in the board's settings. Turn it on if your board has one; the board looks for it after the settings are applied.
sensors.magHint: Knows which way is north. Only some GPS features use it; if you are not sure, leave it as it is.

calibration.warnAngleNoAcc: A mode on your switches (Angle, Horizon, altitude or position hold, GPS Rescue) needs the accelerometer, but this board has no working one. That mode will not work.
calibration.warnGpsNoAcc: The GPS is on, but the accelerometer is off. Some GPS features, like GPS Rescue, need it.

acc.title: Calibrate the accelerometer
acc.step1: Put the quad on a flat, level surface (a table or the floor).
acc.step2: Keep it completely still. Do not touch it or the cable.
acc.step3: Select Calibrate and wait a few seconds.
acc.failedHint: Make sure the quad is level and not moving, then try again.
acc.accOff: Turn the accelerometer on to calibrate it.
acc.optional: Recommended if you use Angle or Horizon mode. You can continue without it.
acc.needed: The board says its accelerometer has not been calibrated yet.
acc.savesNow: The calibration is saved on the board right away, before you apply the other settings.
acc.unsaved: The last apply did not finish, so the board may still have unsaved changes. If calibrating says so, press Reboot board first.
acc.blockedApplying: Settings are being written to the board. Calibrate after that finishes.
acc.blockedPlan: A setup plan is ready but not applied yet. Apply it first, then calibrate.
acc.planDiscarded: You came back after reviewing the plan, so that plan was dropped. Calibrate if you need to; the plan will be made again on the Review step.

orientation.title: Is the board mounted the right way?
orientation.instructions: Hold the quad level. Tilt the nose down, then tilt the right side down, and watch the drone on the screen.
orientation.sideView: From the side (nose on the right)

direction.rightDown: The board says: right side down.
direction.leftDown: The board says: left side down.

orientation.upsideDown: It also thinks it is upside down.
orientation.question: Did the picture move the same way as the quad?
orientation.presetsIntro: Pick how the board's arrow points on the frame. The picture updates right away, so try until tilting matches. The choice is saved when you apply.
orientation.presetsHint: Tilt again after each choice: nose down must show nose down, right side down must show right side down.

presets.roll180yaw90: Upside down, arrow to the right
presets.roll180yaw270: Upside down, arrow to the left

orientation.unavailable: This app version cannot show the board's movement yet. You can skip this check.
orientation.paused: The live view is paused while the board calibrates or restarts.
orientation.busy: The board is busy with another live test. Stop it and try again.
orientation.failed: The live view could not start.
orientation.simulated: This movement is from the demo, not from your board, so the mounting cannot be changed here.
orientation.current: The board is set now to: roll {roll}°, pitch {pitch}°, yaw {yaw}°.
orientation.currentCustom: This is not one of the choices below.
orientation.afterApply: The board itself changes only after you apply the settings. The picture shows the result already.
orientation.stoppedDisconnected: The live view stopped: the board was disconnected. Check the USB cable, then try again.
orientation.stoppedError: The live view stopped: the board stopped answering. Try again.
orientation.view3d: Your drone on the screen, seen from behind. The arrow and the coloured propellers mark the front.
orientation.resetHeadingHint: If the drone on the screen is turned sideways, point your quad away from you and press

calibration.warnAltholdNoBaro: Altitude hold is on a switch, but the barometer is turned off. Without it, altitude hold is much less accurate.

beepers.chooseHint: Starts with Betaflight's beeps, but quiet while the quad is only on USB power.
beepers.keepHint: The wizard does not change the beeps.
beepers.keepOnNote: Lost signal and low battery beeps always stay on: they warn you before the quad falls, and help you find it after a crash.

groupHints.important: Warnings about the radio link, the battery, and arming.

explain.RX_LOST: Beeps when the radio signal is lost, so you can find the quad.
explain.RX_LOST_LANDING: Beeps while the quad lands by itself after losing the signal.
explain.BAT_LOW: Warns that the battery is getting low: time to land.
explain.BAT_CRIT_LOW: Warns that the battery is almost empty: land now.
explain.RX_SET: Beeps when you flip the beeper switch on your radio, to find a lost quad.
explain.ARMING: Beeps when the quad arms, so you know the motors can spin.
explain.ARMED: Reminds you the quad is armed while the throttle is at zero.
explain.GYRO_CALIBRATED: Beeps when the gyro is ready after power on.
explain.ACC_CALIBRATION: Confirms that the level calibration worked.
explain.ACC_CALIBRATION_FAIL: Tells you the level calibration did not work.
explain.ARMING_GPS_FIX: Special arming beep when the GPS has a position.
explain.ARMING_GPS_NO_FIX: Special arming beep when the GPS has no position yet.
explain.GPS_STATUS: Beeps the number of GPS satellites found.
explain.READY_BEEP: Beeps once the quad is ready to arm.
explain.CRASH_FLIP: Beeps while turtle mode is on.
explain.BLACKBOX_ERASE: Confirms that the flight log memory was erased.
explain.RC_SMOOTHING_INIT_FAIL: Warns that radio smoothing could not start (older firmware).
explain.SYSTEM_INIT: Beeps when the board powers on.
explain.ON_USB: Lets the quad beep when it is only powered from USB. Off keeps your desk quiet.
explain.DISARM_REPEAT: Keeps beeping while disarmed with the throttle up.
explain.CAM_CONNECTION_OPEN: Beeps when the camera settings menu opens.
explain.CAM_CONNECTION_CLOSE: Beeps when the camera settings menu closes.
explain.MULTI_BEEPS: Short beeps that confirm a change, for example a new profile chosen with the sticks.

beacon.title: Motor beacon (DShot)
beacon.body: With DShot, the motors themselves can beep. They are much louder than a buzzer, which helps you find a quad that crashed in tall grass. Betaflight has this off by default.

events.RX_LOST: When the radio signal is lost
events.RX_SET: When you turn on the beeper switch

review.clearingsTitle: These ports will be cleared first
review.noClearings: No existing port settings will be cleared.
review.clearingsHint: Only roles the wizard manages are removed. Other port settings stay as they are.
review.nothingWritten: Nothing is written until you select Apply on the next step.
review.planUnavailableTitle: This app version cannot apply settings yet
review.planUnavailableBody: The board connection in this version can only show a preview of the changes, so Apply is turned off. Update the app to apply settings. Nothing has been changed on the board.
review.clearingsUnknown: The ports that will be cleared are shown once the board can prepare the exact changes.
review.unplannedTitle: Some choices cannot be written by this version yet
review.unplannedBody: These choices are not in the list of changes and stay as they are on the board: {list}. Update the app to set them.
review.osdUnplannedTitle: The OSD won't be written yet
review.osdUnplannedBody: This app version can't save the OSD layout to the board yet. Your other settings will be applied as normal.

apply.doNotUnplug: Do not unplug the board until this finishes.
apply.verifying: Checking the settings on the board…
apply.verified: All settings were saved and checked.
apply.notSaved: The settings were sent but not saved. Nothing changed on the board.
apply.failedHint: A backup was made before applying. You can restore it below.

mismatch.title: Some settings did not stick
mismatch.body: The board was read back after saving, and these values are different:
mismatch.step1: Select Apply again. A second try often fixes it.
mismatch.step2: If the same setting fails again, your firmware may not support it. Update the firmware and try again.
mismatch.step3: You can restore the backup below to undo all changes.

apply.notReconnected: The settings were saved, but the board did not reconnect by itself. Check the USB cable, then connect again to check them.

done.next1: Bind your receiver to your radio if you have not already.
done.next2: Check that the arm switch and modes react on your radio.
done.next3: Do a short hover test outdoors, away from people.
done.linkIssues: Report a problem with the wizard

backups.title: Backups
backups.intro: Backups for this board, newest first.
backups.sessionOnly: Backups made in this session. Older backups are in the backups folder.
backups.folderFallback: The folder could not be opened. It is here:
backups.confirmBody: All settings on the board are replaced with the backup from {date}. The board restarts.

ports.noneFree: No free port. Free one up on another step, or check the wiring.

question.vtx: Which UART is the video transmitter wired to?
question.gps: Which UART is the GPS wired to?
question.escTelemetry: Which UART is the ESC telemetry wire on?

wiring.vtx: The VTX control wire goes to the UART TX pad.
wiring.gps: GPS TX goes to the UART RX pad, GPS RX to TX.
wiring.escTelemetry: The ESC telemetry wire goes to the UART RX pad.

validation.firmwareUnsupported: Update the firmware to Betaflight {min} or newer.
validation.firmwareDecide: Choose to update or keep the current firmware.
validation.noConfig: The board did not report its ports. Reconnect and try again.
validation.receiverRequired: Choose a receiver. You need one to fly.
validation.noOnboardReceiver: This board has no built-in receiver.
validation.vtxProtocolRequired: Choose how the video transmitter is controlled.
validation.portConflict: {role}: {port} cannot be used. Choose another port.
validation.bidirNeedsDshot: Bidirectional DShot needs a DShot protocol.
validation.motorPolesInvalid: Motor poles must be an even number between 2 and 64.
validation.armAlwaysOn: The arm switch needs an off position.
validation.armOverlap: Arm and {mode} use the same switch position.
validation.modeUnknown: {mode} is not a mode this wizard can set.
validation.modeNeedsFirmware: {mode} needs Betaflight {version} or newer. Remove it or update the firmware.
validation.elrsArmAux1: With ExpressLRS, arm must be on AUX1.
validation.modeRangeInvalid: The switch position for {mode} is not valid.
validation.auxInvalid: The switch channel for {mode} is not valid.
validation.notGenerated: Wait for the preview to finish.
validation.notApplied: Apply the settings and wait for the check to finish.
validation.planUnavailable: This app version cannot apply settings yet. Update the app.
validation.crsfFamilyRequired: Choose which radio system the receiver uses.
validation.bindingRequired: Choose how to bind the receiver.
validation.phraseNotSet: Enter the binding phrase and press “Use this phrase”, or bind with the button.
validation.prearmSameSwitch: Prearm must be on a different switch than arm.
validation.turtleNeedsDshot: Turtle mode needs the DShot ESC protocol. Change the ESC protocol, or remove turtle mode.
validation.airmodeSwitchMissing: Air mode is set to "on a switch": add the switch.
validation.calibrationRunning: Wait until the calibration is finished.
validation.beepersChoose: Choose the recommended beeps, or keep the current ones.
validation.accNeededByModes: The accelerometer is turned off, but these switches need it: {modes}. Turn the accelerometer on, or remove those switches.
validation.alignmentInvalid: The board mounting angles must be whole degrees from -180 to 360.

validation.osdLayout: The default OSD layout hasn't loaded. Try again, or keep the current OSD.
validation.osdHdUnsupported: The firmware on this board can't show the OSD in digital goggles. Pick an analog option, keep the board's current OSD, or flash firmware with the "OSD (HD)" option.
validation.rxOptionMissing: The firmware on this board doesn't include this receiver protocol. Pick another one or update the firmware.

validation.rxOptionMissingNoUpdate: {rxProtocol} isn't in the firmware on this board, and the firmware can't be updated right now. Pick another protocol to continue.
validation.firmwareNotSupportedYet: The wizard can't set up Betaflight {version} yet. Install one of the versions offered on this step.

BOARD_NOT_FOUND.title: No flight controller found
BOARD_NOT_FOUND.body: The computer does not see a flight controller. This is usually the cable or the USB port.
BOARD_NOT_FOUND.step1: Check that the USB cable is pushed in firmly at both ends. Wait a few seconds.
BOARD_NOT_FOUND.step2: Try another cable. Many USB cables only charge.
BOARD_NOT_FOUND.step3: Plug straight into the computer, not through a hub.
BOARD_NOT_FOUND.step4: Check that a light turns on on the board. If nothing lights up, it is not getting power.

PORT_BUSY.title: The flight controller's connection is in use
PORT_BUSY.body: Another program, or another window of this app, has the connection open.
PORT_BUSY.step1: Close other windows of this app, and apps such as Betaflight Configurator or Cura.
PORT_BUSY.step2: Wait a few seconds, then try again.

PORT_BUSY_APP.title: This app is already using the flight controller
PORT_BUSY_APP.body: Another window of this app, or a task still running here (such as a motor test or the live switch check), has the connection.
PORT_BUSY_APP.step1: Close the other window of this app, or finish what it is doing.

PORT_BUSY_EXTERNAL.title: Another program is using the flight controller
PORT_BUSY_EXTERNAL.body: Another app on this computer has the connection open.
PORT_BUSY_EXTERNAL.step1: Close Betaflight Configurator, Cura or another app that may use the port (for example ESC Configurator or a 3D-printer tool).
PORT_BUSY_EXTERNAL.step2: Wait a few seconds, then try again.

DISCONNECTED.title: The flight controller was disconnected
DISCONNECTED.body: The connection to the board was lost.
DISCONNECTED.step1: Check that the USB cable is firmly plugged in.
DISCONNECTED.step2: Select Reconnect. Your answers so far are kept.

TIMEOUT.title: The flight controller stopped responding
TIMEOUT.body: The board did not answer in time.
TIMEOUT.step1: Check the cable, then select Try again.
TIMEOUT.step2: If it keeps happening, try another USB port or cable.

SERIAL_ERROR.title: Could not talk to the board
SERIAL_ERROR.body: The USB connection reported an error.
SERIAL_ERROR.step1: Check the USB cable and that the board is powered, then try again.
SERIAL_ERROR.step2: Try another USB port or cable.

DRIVER_MISSING.title: Windows needs a driver for this board
DRIVER_MISSING.body: Windows sees the board but has no driver for it. This is common on a new computer.
DRIVER_MISSING.step1: Select Install the driver. It takes a minute.
DRIVER_MISSING.step2: When it is installed, try again.

USB_ERROR.title: USB error
USB_ERROR.body: The computer reported a USB problem while talking to the board.
USB_ERROR.step1: Check the USB cable and that the board is powered, then try again.
USB_ERROR.step2: Try another USB port, straight on the computer.

UNSUPPORTED_FIRMWARE.title: The wizard can't set up this firmware version
UNSUPPORTED_FIRMWARE.body: This version of the wizard can't set up the Betaflight version on this board.
UNSUPPORTED_FIRMWARE.step1: Go to the firmware step and install a version the wizard offers.

MSP_UNSUPPORTED.title: The board does not support this
MSP_UNSUPPORTED.body: The firmware on the board does not know this request.
MSP_UNSUPPORTED.step1: Update the firmware and try again.

MSP_BAD_RESPONSE.title: Unexpected answer from the board
MSP_BAD_RESPONSE.body: The board sent an answer the wizard did not understand.
MSP_BAD_RESPONSE.step1: Try again. If it repeats, reconnect the board.

CLI_ERROR.title: The board rejected a command
CLI_ERROR.body: A settings command failed on the board. The board message is shown below.
CLI_ERROR.step1: Try again. If the same command fails, report the problem.

DFU_NOT_FOUND.title: The board did not enter flashing mode
DFU_NOT_FOUND.body: The board restarts into a special mode (DFU) to install firmware. It did not show up in that mode.
DFU_NOT_FOUND.step2: If that fails, the DFU driver may be missing. Select Install the driver.
DFU_NOT_FOUND.step3: Or unplug the board, hold the BOOT button, plug it in while holding it, then release.

FLASH_FAILED.title: The firmware install did not finish
FLASH_FAILED.body: Something interrupted the install. The board is not damaged and you can flash again.
FLASH_FAILED.step1: Leave the board plugged in and do not touch the cable.
FLASH_FAILED.step3: If it fails again, try another cable and port.

VERIFY_MISMATCH.title: The firmware check failed
VERIFY_MISMATCH.body: The firmware read back from the board does not match what was written.
VERIFY_MISMATCH.step1: Select Flash again with full erase.
VERIFY_MISMATCH.step2: If it fails again, try another cable and port.

READ_PROTECTED.title: The board is read protected
READ_PROTECTED.body: The chip is locked, so new firmware cannot be written. Nothing was erased.
READ_PROTECTED.step1: Removing the lock erases the whole chip, including all settings. The wizard asks before doing it.
READ_PROTECTED.step2: If you are unsure, unplug the board and ask for help.

REPLUG_REQUIRED.title: Unplug and replug the board
REPLUG_REQUIRED.body: The board needs a fresh start to continue.
REPLUG_REQUIRED.step1: Unplug the USB cable, wait 3 seconds and plug it back in.

FIRMWARE_TOO_LARGE.title: The firmware does not fit
FIRMWARE_TOO_LARGE.body: This firmware is too large for the board.
FIRMWARE_TOO_LARGE.step1: Choose another version, or report the problem.

INVALID_FIRMWARE.title: The firmware file is not valid
INVALID_FIRMWARE.body: The firmware file is damaged or not for this board.
INVALID_FIRMWARE.step1: Try again. The file is downloaded again.

NO_FLASH_LAYOUT.title: Unknown memory layout
NO_FLASH_LAYOUT.body: The wizard does not know how to flash this chip.
NO_FLASH_LAYOUT.step1: Report the problem with the technical details.

NETWORK_ERROR.title: No internet connection
NETWORK_ERROR.body: The wizard could not reach the Betaflight servers.
NETWORK_ERROR.step1: Check that the computer is online.

BUILD_API_ERROR.title: The build server had a problem
BUILD_API_ERROR.body: The Betaflight build server returned an error.
BUILD_API_ERROR.step1: Wait a minute and try again.

BUILD_FAILED.title: The firmware build failed
BUILD_FAILED.body: The build server could not build firmware for this board. The server message is shown below.
BUILD_FAILED.step1: Choose another version, or report the problem.

IO_ERROR.title: Could not read or write a file
IO_ERROR.body: A file on this computer could not be read or written.
IO_ERROR.step1: Check that the disk is not full, then try again.

DATA_ERROR.title: Unexpected data
DATA_ERROR.body: Some data could not be read.
DATA_ERROR.step1: Try again. If it repeats, report the problem.

MOTOR_TEST_REFUSED.title: The motor test was not started
MOTOR_TEST_REFUSED.body: Safety checks stopped the motor test. The reason is shown below.
MOTOR_TEST_REFUSED.step1: Confirm that the propellers are removed and the battery is connected, then try again.

BOARD_ARMED.title: The board is armed
BOARD_ARMED.body: This cannot be done while the board is armed (motor test or calibration).
BOARD_ARMED.step1: Flip the arm switch on your radio to off.

MOTOR_TEST_NOT_ACTIVE.title: The motor test stopped
MOTOR_TEST_NOT_ACTIVE.body: The motors stopped on their own, for safety.
MOTOR_TEST_NOT_ACTIVE.step1: Start the test again if needed.

CANCELLED.title: Cancelled
CANCELLED.step1: Start it again when you are ready.

BUSY.title: Please wait
BUSY.step1: Wait for it to finish, then try again.

INVALID_ARGUMENT.title: Invalid request
INVALID_ARGUMENT.body: The wizard sent something the app could not use.
INVALID_ARGUMENT.step1: Report the problem with the technical details.

INTERNAL.title: Something went wrong
INTERNAL.body: An unexpected error happened in the app.
INTERNAL.step1: Report the problem with the technical details.

NOT_IMPLEMENTED.title: Not available yet
NOT_IMPLEMENTED.body: This part of the app is not finished yet.
NOT_IMPLEMENTED.step1: You can skip it for now.

UNKNOWN.title: Something went wrong
UNKNOWN.step1: Try again. If it repeats, report the problem.

CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED.title: The board cannot use part of this setup
CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED.body: The flight controller does not support something you chose, most often the receiver type.
CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED.step1: Go back to Components and choose a different receiver, for example one wired to a UART.
CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED.step2: If the board has a built-in receiver and you still see this, report the problem and include the details below.

MIXED_BACKEND.title: Blocked: simulated and real data were mixed
MIXED_BACKEND.body: Part of this step was prepared by the simulation (demo mode) while your flight controller is real, or the other way round. Writing it could put made-up settings or firmware on a real board, so the app stopped. Nothing was written to the board.
MIXED_BACKEND.step1: To finish on your real flight controller, update the app to a version that can do every step for real, then start again.
MIXED_BACKEND.step2: To just explore the wizard, close the app, start it without a board connected and choose “Try the demo”.

ACC_NOT_AVAILABLE.title: No accelerometer found
ACC_NOT_AVAILABLE.body: The board did not find an accelerometer, so there is nothing to calibrate.
ACC_NOT_AVAILABLE.step1: Some small or racing boards have no accelerometer. That is fine for Acro flying.
ACC_NOT_AVAILABLE.step2: Skip the calibration. Angle and Horizon modes will not work without it.

ACC_NOT_AVAILABLE_OFF.title: The accelerometer is turned off
ACC_NOT_AVAILABLE_OFF.body: The accelerometer is turned off in the board's settings, so it cannot be calibrated now.
ACC_NOT_AVAILABLE_OFF.step1: Turn the accelerometer on above and apply the settings.
ACC_NOT_AVAILABLE_OFF.step2: Then come back and calibrate it.

BOARD_MOVING.title: The quad is moving
BOARD_MOVING.body: The quad must be completely still to calibrate. Nothing was changed.
BOARD_MOVING.step1: Keep it still: put the quad on a table, and let go of it and the cable.

BOARD_MOVING_DURING.title: The quad moved while calibrating
BOARD_MOVING_DURING.body: The quad moved during the calibration, so the result is not good.
BOARD_MOVING_DURING.step1: Put the quad down on a flat, level surface and do not touch it or the cable.

ACC_CALIBRATION_FAILED.title: The calibration did not finish
ACC_CALIBRATION_FAILED.body: The board did not finish calibrating the accelerometer.
ACC_CALIBRATION_FAILED.step1: Keep the quad level and still, and try again.
ACC_CALIBRATION_FAILED.step2: If it fails again, check the USB cable and that the board is powered, then try once more.

PENDING_UNSAVED_CHANGES.title: The board has unsaved changes
PENDING_UNSAVED_CHANGES.body: The board has changes that were never saved, and calibrating now would save them too. Press Reboot board first: the board will restart and nothing unsaved will be kept.
PENDING_UNSAVED_CHANGES.step1: Press Reboot board. Your saved settings stay as they are; only the unsaved changes are dropped. Nothing was calibrated.
PENDING_UNSAVED_CHANGES.step2: When the board is back, calibrate again.

REBOOT_NOT_CONFIRMED.title: We couldn't confirm the board restarted
REBOOT_NOT_CONFIRMED.body: We couldn't confirm the board restarted, so the unsaved changes may still be there. Press Reboot board again. If it keeps failing, check the USB cable and that the board is powered.
REBOOT_NOT_CONFIRMED.step1: Press Reboot board again. It is safe to press it more than once.
REBOOT_NOT_CONFIRMED.step2: If it keeps failing, check the USB cable and that the board is powered.

REBOOT_BOARD_LOST.title: The board didn't come back after restarting
REBOOT_BOARD_LOST.body: The board didn't come back after restarting. Check the USB cable, then connect again. After you reconnect, Reboot board is still the way to clear the unsaved changes.
REBOOT_BOARD_LOST.step1: Check the USB cable and that the board is powered.
REBOOT_BOARD_LOST.step2: Go to Connect and connect again. If calibrating still says there are unsaved changes, press Reboot board.

LIVE_VIEW_BUSY.title: The board is busy
LIVE_VIEW_BUSY.body: The board was still busy with the live view, so nothing was started. Wait a moment, then try again.

CONNECT_REBOOT_NOT_CONFIRMED.title: We couldn't confirm the board restarted
CONNECT_REBOOT_NOT_CONFIRMED.body: This board still had unsaved changes, so it is restarted when you connect, but we couldn't confirm the restart. Try connecting again. If it keeps failing, check the USB cable and that the board is powered.
CONNECT_REBOOT_NOT_CONFIRMED.step1: Select Try again. It is safe to try more than once.
CONNECT_REBOOT_NOT_CONFIRMED.step2: If it keeps failing, check the USB cable and that the board is powered.

OSD_HD_UNSUPPORTED.title: The firmware on this board can't show the OSD in digital goggles
OSD_HD_UNSUPPORTED.body: You chose the digital HD OSD, but the firmware on this board was built without it, so the setup plan couldn't be made. Nothing was changed on the board.
OSD_HD_UNSUPPORTED.step1: Select Back to OSD settings, then pick an analog option or keep the board's current OSD.
OSD_HD_UNSUPPORTED.step2: To use the OSD in digital goggles, go back to OSD settings and select Update the firmware to add this, or flash firmware built with the "OSD (HD)" option, then come back to Review.

BUILD_OPTIONS_UNAVAILABLE.title: Couldn't reach the Betaflight build server
BUILD_OPTIONS_UNAVAILABLE.body: We need the list of features for Betaflight {release} to build the firmware, but the build server didn't answer. Nothing was changed on the board.
BUILD_OPTIONS_UNAVAILABLE.step1: Check that this computer is connected to the internet.

REQUIRED_OPTION_UNSUPPORTED.title: This firmware version can't include what you chose
REQUIRED_OPTION_UNSUPPORTED.body: Betaflight {release} can't be built with: {options}. Nothing was changed on the board.
REQUIRED_OPTION_UNSUPPORTED.step1: Pick another firmware version in the list above, then try again.

driverReplace.title: Installing the driver replaces another driver
driverReplace.body: {device} currently uses the {driver} driver. Installing the WinUSB driver replaces it, so this app and Betaflight can flash the board.
driverReplace.tools: Programs that rely on the old driver may stop seeing the board in bootloader mode, for example STM32CubeProgrammer or DfuSe with ST's STTub30 driver.
driverReplace.undo: If you need those programs again, reinstall their driver from their installer. Nothing changes on the flight controller itself.
driverReplace.understand: I understand that the {driver} driver will be replaced by WinUSB.

osd.intro: The OSD (on-screen display) is the text drawn over your camera picture: battery, flight time, warnings and more. Pick only what you need, so the picture stays clear.

system.title: Your video system

detected.AUTO: Your video transmitter is analog, so the screen is 4:3. The OSD is set to Auto: it matches your camera (PAL or NTSC) by itself.
detected.HD: Your video transmitter is digital HD (DJI, Walksnail or HDZero), so the screen is widescreen 16:9.

system.ask: We couldn't tell which video system you have. Which one do you use?
system.HDHint: DJI O3/O4, Walksnail Avatar or HDZero: a sharp, widescreen picture.
system.AUTOHint: Matches your camera by itself, PAL or NTSC. Pick this if you're not sure.
system.PALHint: Only if your camera is set to PAL. It gives a few more lines of text.
system.NTSCHint: Only if your camera is set to NTSC.
system.hdUnsupported: Not available: the firmware on this board can't show the OSD in digital goggles. You can update the firmware to add it (the "OSD (HD)" option).
system.hdBlocked: Your video transmitter is digital HD, but the firmware on this board can't show the OSD in digital goggles (it was built without the HD OSD).
system.analogOnDigital: Your video transmitter is digital, but the OSD is set to analog. The text may not show in your goggles. Pick Digital HD unless you're sure.
system.hdRejected: The setup plan found that the firmware on this board can't show the OSD in digital goggles (it was built without the HD OSD).
system.hdChoices: You can update the firmware to add the HD OSD (the "OSD (HD)" option), keep the OSD that is on the board now, or pick an analog option below if your goggles show analog video.
system.kept: The board's current OSD stays as it is. Nothing about the OSD will be changed.
system.hdUnknown: We couldn't confirm that the firmware on this board can show the OSD in digital goggles. You can still pick HD. If the Review step says it's missing, flash firmware built with the "OSD (HD)" option.

osd.chooseHint: Start from a recommended layout and adjust it.
osd.keepHint: Leave the OSD on the board as it is.

AVG_CELL_VOLTAGE.label: Battery voltage per cell
AVG_CELL_VOLTAGE.hint: The best way to know when to land: land at about 3.5 V per cell.

MAIN_BATT_VOLTAGE.label: Total battery voltage
MAIN_BATT_VOLTAGE.hint: The whole pack's voltage. Per-cell voltage is easier to read.

MAH_DRAWN.label: Battery used (mAh)
MAH_DRAWN.hint: How much of the battery you've used so far.

ITEM_TIMER_2.label: Flight timer
ITEM_TIMER_2.hint: How long you've been flying on this battery.

LINK_QUALITY.label: Radio link quality
LINK_QUALITY.hint: How well the drone hears your radio. Turn back if it drops.

WARNINGS.label: Warnings
WARNINGS.hint: Short alerts such as low battery or a lost radio signal.

CRAFT_NAME.label: Drone name
CRAFT_NAME.hint: The name you gave this drone.

GPS_SATS.label: GPS satellites
GPS_SATS.hint: How many satellites the GPS sees. Wait for enough before you take off.

HOME_DIR.label: Arrow to home
HOME_DIR.hint: Points back to where you took off.

HOME_DIST.label: Distance to home
HOME_DIST.hint: How far you are from where you took off.

RSSI_VALUE.label: Signal strength (%)
RSSI_VALUE.hint: The radio signal as a percentage. Link quality is usually more useful.

RSSI_DBM_VALUE.label: Signal strength (dBm)
RSSI_DBM_VALUE.hint: The radio signal in dBm, for ELRS and Crossfire.

THROTTLE_POS.label: Throttle
THROTTLE_POS.hint: How much throttle you're giving, in percent.

CURRENT_DRAW.label: Current draw
CURRENT_DRAW.hint: How many amps the motors are pulling right now.

FLYMODE.label: Flight mode
FLYMODE.hint: The current flight mode, such as ACRO or ANGLE.

CROSSHAIRS.label: Crosshair
CROSSHAIRS.hint: A small mark in the middle of the screen.

ITEM_TIMER_1.label: Total on-time
ITEM_TIMER_1.hint: How long the drone has been powered on.

DISARMED.label: DISARMED label
DISARMED.hint: Shows DISARMED in the middle while the motors are off.

ESC_TMP.label: ESC temperature
ESC_TMP.hint: How hot the ESC is. Needs ESC telemetry.

osd.moveLabel: {item}: drag, or use the arrow keys to move
osd.previewHint: Preview with sample values ({cols} × {rows} grid). Drag an item, or select it and use the arrow keys.

reflash.offer: Update the firmware to add this
reflash.confirmTitle: Update the firmware on this board?
reflash.confirmBody: The board will restart into update mode and the new firmware will be written. First, a backup of its current settings is saved.
reflash.confirmKeep: Your answers in this wizard are kept, and afterwards you come back to this step.
reflash.blockedApplied: Updating the firmware isn't available any more: settings were already written to the board in this session. To add this, finish here, update the firmware, then run the wizard again.
reflash.blockedMixed: Updating the firmware isn't available: part of the data here is simulated and the board is real.
reflash.banner: Updating the firmware to add what you chose on the {step} step. Pick a version and select Update; afterwards you go back to {step}.

flashOptions.title: Update options
flashOptions.keepHelp: Before the update, the wizard saves a backup of the board's settings. When the new firmware is installed, it puts those settings back. This matters even without erasing the chip: moving to a different version line (for example from 4.4 to 4.5) starts the board with default settings.
flashOptions.keepOffHelp: When this is off, the wizard doesn't put your settings back. A normal update within the same version line keeps them on the board (so does going between 4.5 and 2025.12). Moving to another version line, or erasing the whole chip, starts from default settings. Your backup is still saved in the Backups list.
flashOptions.eraseHelp: Wipes the board's memory completely before the new firmware is written. Use it if an earlier update failed or the board acts strangely. The erase alone can take up to about 30 seconds.
flashOptions.warnEraseKeep: The chip is wiped fully, then your saved settings are put back.
flashOptions.warnEraseReset: Everything on the board resets to default settings. If the board had Betaflight, your backup is still saved in the Backups list.
flashOptions.warnCrossLine: Your settings come from Betaflight {from} and you're installing {to}, a different version line. Some settings may not carry over cleanly; the wizard asks again for what's needed.
flashOptions.warnLineReset: Betaflight {to} stores settings differently from {from}, so the board starts with default settings after this update, even without erasing the chip. Turn on “Keep my settings” to put your settings back.
flashOptions.eraseWait: Erasing the whole chip can take up to about 30 seconds. Keep the board plugged in.

progress.RESTORING: Putting your settings back: line {line} of {total}…
progress.SAVING: Saving the settings on the board…

restore.doneBody: {n} settings from your backup were put back on the new firmware.
restore.notSaved: The board did not save the settings. Restore your backup from the Backups list, or set the board up again in the next steps.
restore.lineChanged: Your settings came from Betaflight {from}. The board now runs {to}, where some settings work differently. The wizard asks again for what's needed in the next steps.
restore.failedTitle: Settings the new firmware didn't accept ({n})
restore.failedHelp: The board refused these lines from your backup. Each one is shown exactly as the board answered. The wizard asks again for what's needed.
restore.skippedHelp: These lines were not sent because they don't fit the new firmware. The reason is next to each one.
restore.warningsHelp: Things to know about the restore:

skip.COMMENT: A note in the backup file, not a setting.
skip.SESSION_CONTROL: A control line; the wizard sends its own.
skip.BOARD_IDENTITY: The board's own name and ID. They belong to this board, so they are never copied from a backup.
skip.HARDWARE_LINE_CHANGED: Which pin does what (motors, LEDs and so on) is set up differently in the new firmware version, so the new firmware's own pin setup for this board is used instead.
skip.REMOVED_ON_TARGET: The new firmware version doesn't have this setting any more, so there was nothing to copy it to.
skip.NOT_IN_BUILD: The new firmware version has this setting, but the firmware built for your board left that feature out.
skip.SEMANTICS_CHANGED: This setting has the same name but works differently in the new firmware version, so copying the old number could change how the quad flies. Set it again yourself (see the notes below).
skip.NO_EQUIVALENT_MODE: This switch mode or in-flight adjustment doesn't exist in the new firmware version, so it was left out.
skip.PORT_NOT_AVAILABLE: This connector (serial port) isn't available on your board with the new firmware, so its setting was left out.
skip.OTHER_BATTERY_PROFILE: This came from one of your other battery profiles. The new firmware version has only one set of battery settings, so only the battery profile you were using was copied.

restore.skipUnknown: This line was not copied to the new firmware. (Reason code: {code})

note.CONVERTED: Your settings were converted from Betaflight {from} to {to}. Look through the lines that were left out.
note.D_TERM: Your D settings were not copied. D is the part of the PID tuning that calms down wobbles, and Betaflight 2025.12 changed what its numbers mean. Before you fly, set your D values again or load your tune again. Until then the new firmware's default D values are used.
note.BATTERY_INTO_PROFILE: Your battery settings ({settings}) were copied into battery profile {profile}, the one in use. The other battery profiles keep their default values.
note.OTHER_BATTERY_PROFILE: Only battery profile {profile} was copied, because Betaflight {to} has just one set of battery settings.
note.SERIAL_FUNCTIONS_REMOVED: Some uses of the serial ports don't exist in Betaflight {to}, so they were removed: {ports}.
note.MATCHED_BY_NAME: The board's unique ID couldn't be read, so the backup was matched by the board name ({board}) only.
note.READ_BACK_FAILED: After the board restarted, the wizard couldn't read the settings back to double-check them.
note.READ_BACK_DIFFERS: After the board restarted, {name} didn't read back the way it was restored. Check it in the next steps.

restore.refusedTitle: The firmware is installed, but your settings were not put back

refused.BOARD_UID_MISMATCH: The backup belongs to a different board, so it wasn't used.
refused.BACKUP_NOT_DIFF_ALL: The backup isn't a complete copy of the settings, so it wasn't used.
refused.BACKUP_UNREADABLE: The backup file couldn't be read.
refused.BOARD_NOT_RECONNECTED: The board stopped answering while the settings were being put back.
refused.UNSUPPORTED_FIRMWARE: The wizard can't put settings back on this Betaflight version yet.
refused.NOT_AVAILABLE: This version of the app can't put settings back after an update yet.
refused.GENERIC: Something went wrong while putting the settings back.

refusedStage.NOTHING_SENT: Nothing was changed on the board.
refusedStage.RESTORING: The settings were not saved, so the board has the new firmware's default settings.
refusedStage.SAVING: It isn't known whether the settings were saved.
refusedStage.REBOOTING: The settings were saved, but the wizard couldn't check them.

restore.backupSaved: Your backup is saved and listed under Backups:
restore.noBackup: No backup was taken during this update (the board was already in flashing mode), so there were no settings to put back.
